correctness.rationale: The ring is Z; residue classes index the rows and columns, not the entries' arithmetic. Grouping indices modulo p gives G_p=cI+b(I_p⊗J_p)+J_{p²} with b=p−1 and c=pb. In the presentation, subtracting the first relation in each block leaves c times each difference generator; the primitive sum of these differences is the only coupled coordinate. This splits off p(p−2) copies of c. In the integral basis consisting of e_1, the primitive kernel vector Σ_{i>1}(e_i−e_1), and a kernel complement, J_p acts by the displayed 2×2 block plus zero. It gives p−2 blocks with entry gcd b and determinant 2c², hence factors b and 2p²b. Pivoting on the 1 in the 4×4 block leaves bT_p; T_p has entry gcd 1, every 2×2 minor a multiple of p² with one equal to p², and determinant 2p⁴(3p−2). The resulting factors combine in the asserted divisibility order, with p=2 giving 1,1,4,32. A separate exact Smith computation on the full integer matrices agrees at p=2,3,5; replay: python3 /workspace/branches/f355b5e8-f250-4436-ba9a-0e5e54520ac2/independent_snf.py. These finite cases corroborate the integral proof; they are not an argument for arbitrary primes.
